# ARTICLE 10 — CONSTRUCTION COVENANTS

## Section 10.1 Commencement and Continuity of Construction

Borrower shall cause construction of the Project to commence not later than thirty (30) days after the Closing Date and to be prosecuted diligently and continuously, in a good and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the Plans and Specifications, the GMP Contract, the Approved Budget, all applicable permits and Legal Requirements, and the approved construction schedule. Borrower shall not suspend or abandon construction for more than fifteen (15) consecutive days (other than as a result of an Unavoidable Delay that is not caused by Borrower, the Contractor or any Affiliate of either, and as to which Borrower has delivered prior written notice to Lender).

## Section 10.2 Plans and Specifications

Lender has reviewed and approved the Plans and Specifications identified in **Schedule 10.2** for purposes of this Agreement only. Borrower shall not modify the Plans and Specifications in any material respect, and shall not permit any material deviation from the Plans and Specifications, without Lender's prior written consent. For purposes of this Section, a modification is "material" if it (a) changes the number or mix of residential units or the amount of retail square footage; (b) changes the building footprint, height, structural system, exterior materials or parking count; (c) relocates any residential occupancy space into or above the Affected Area; (d) changes the scope or design of the Vapor Mitigation System; (e) would require any rezoning, variance, special use permit or other discretionary approval; (f) would require any additional approval of the Brightleaf Historic District Association Architectural Review Committee; or (g) increases hard costs by more than $500,000 in the aggregate.

## Section 10.3 GMP Contract; Change Orders

(a) Borrower shall not amend, modify, terminate, replace or assign the GMP Contract (other than the collateral assignment to Lender) without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall cause the Contractor to perform in accordance with the GMP Contract, and shall enforce the GMP Contract for the benefit of Lender.

(b) Borrower may approve individual change orders that, in the aggregate with all other change orders, do not exceed $250,000 and do not constitute a material modification under **Section 10.2** without Lender's consent, provided that (i) such change orders are funded from the contingency line item of the Approved Budget or from Equity Contributions, (ii) Borrower delivers a copy of each such change order to Lender within ten (10) Business Days, and (iii) no such change order reduces the scope of the Project or the quality of the work. All other change orders require Lender's prior written consent ("**Approved Change Orders**").

(c) Borrower shall deliver to Lender, within ten (10) days after execution, a copy of each Approved Change Order, together with the Contractor's and Architect's certification of the resulting contract amount and schedule impact.

(d) Borrower shall not permit the aggregate of the GMP Contract amount plus all Approved Change Orders to exceed the hard cost line items of the Approved Budget unless the excess is funded from the contingency line item or from Equity Contributions deposited with Lender.

## Section 10.4 Contractor and Architect Requirements

(a) Borrower shall not terminate, replace or substitute the Contractor or the Architect without Lender's prior written consent. Any replacement contractor or architect must be approved by Lender and must satisfy the requirements of this Section.

(b) Borrower shall cause the Contractor to (i) maintain its North Carolina general contractor's license in good standing, (ii) maintain the insurance required under **Article 20** and the GMP Contract, (iii) deliver payment and performance bonds in the full amount of the GMP Contract (100%) from a surety acceptable to Lender and rated at least A- by A.M. Best, unless waived by Lender in writing, and (iv) deliver, within thirty (30) days after the Closing Date, its audited or reviewed financial statements for the two most recent fiscal years and a statement of bonding capacity. The requirement for payment and performance bonds shall be a condition to the first Progress Advance.

(c) Borrower shall cause the Architect to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per claim, and to deliver a collateral assignment of the Architect's Agreement, together with consents to assignment from the Contractor and the Architect.

## Section 10.5 Construction Schedule; Construction Delay Default

Borrower has delivered the baseline construction schedule approved by Lender (the "**Baseline Schedule**"), which reflects a Projected Substantial Completion Date of August 31, 2027. Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Construction Maturity Date of August 28, 2027 precedes the Projected Substantial Completion Date of August 31, 2027, and (b) accordingly the Loan contemplates that Substantial Completion may occur during the Mini-Perm Period. Borrower shall deliver an updated construction schedule with each monthly progress report. If at any time the Project is more than ninety (90) days behind the Baseline Schedule (as adjusted for Approved Change Orders and Unavoidable Delays), a Construction Delay Default shall exist under **Section 24.9**.

## Section 10.6 Compliance with Legal Requirements; Permits

Borrower shall comply, and shall cause the Contractor and the Architect to comply, with all Legal Requirements applicable to the Property, the Project and the construction, including all building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, energy, zoning, stormwater, sedimentation and Environmental Laws. Borrower shall obtain and maintain all permits, licenses, approvals and certificates required for the construction and occupancy of the Project, including the building permits, the certificates of occupancy, the Zoning Report, the right-of-way and utility approvals, and all approvals required under the Brightleaf Historic District Association Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, as amended by the First Amendment recorded in Book 7102, Page 388, Durham County Registry (the "**CC&Rs**").

## Section 10.7 Brightleaf Historic District Architectural Review

Borrower shall, as a condition to Closing and thereafter as a continuing covenant, (a) submit the final Plans and Specifications to the Brightleaf Historic District Association Architectural Review Committee in accordance with Article V of the CC&Rs, and (b) obtain the written approval of the Architectural Review Committee (or the lapse of the sixty (60) day deemed-approval period under Section 5 of the CC&Rs without written action). Borrower shall deliver evidence of such approval to Lender not later than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date. Borrower shall comply with the architectural review and design standards of the CC&Rs and with the assessment obligations thereunder, which Borrower acknowledges are currently assessed at $0.12 per square foot of gross building area per annum (approximately $34,500 per annum for the Project) and are not separately identified as a line item in the Appraisal's operating expense projection. Any modification to the Plans and Specifications requiring architectural review committee approval shall not be implemented until such approval is obtained.

## Section 10.8 Close-Out Deliverables

Upon Substantial Completion, and as a condition to the release of Retainage, Borrower shall deliver to Lender: (a) the final, unconditional certificate of occupancy for all residential units, retail bays and the parking garage; (b) the Architect's certificate of final completion; (c) as-built Plans and Specifications and CAD files; (d) all warranties, guaranties, operating manuals, attic stock and training materials, together with assignments of all contractor and manufacturer warranties; (e) final, unconditional lien waivers and releases from the Contractor, the Architect, all subcontractors and all materialmen; (f) an updated ALTA/NSPS Survey showing the Project as built, with no encroachments or survey defects other than those approved by Lender; (g) evidence that all punchlist items have been completed; (h) evidence of final inspection sign-off by the City of Durham and the fire marshal; (i) evidence of compliance with the life-safety, accessibility and energy-code requirements; and (j) such other close-out items as Lender may reasonably require.

## Section 10.9 Leasing and Stabilization

From and after Substantial Completion, Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to lease the Project to Stabilization, shall lease the Property in accordance with the Approved Leasing Guidelines (as approved by Lender prior to the first lease), and shall not enter into any lease of more than 5,000 square feet of retail space, any lease with a term (including options) exceeding fifteen (15) years, any lease requiring landlord construction work in excess of $250,000, or any lease that is not on arm's-length terms without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall deliver the Rent Roll and a leasing status report with each quarterly report delivered under **Article 23**.

## Section 10.10 Defects; Corrective Work

Borrower shall promptly correct, or cause the Contractor to correct, any Defect in the Project. If Borrower fails to do so within thirty (30) days after notice from Lender (or such longer period as is reasonably necessary provided Borrower is diligently pursuing cure), Lender may perform such work as a protective advance under **Section 9.10**, and the cost thereof shall be an Obligation.

# ARTICLE 11 — APPROVED BUDGET; SOURCES AND USES; EQUITY

## Section 11.1 Approved Budget

The Approved Budget is attached as **Exhibit B** and reflects Total Project Costs of $56,700,000, comprising land acquisition of $8,200,000, hard construction costs of $34,750,000, soft costs of $4,150,000, the Interest Reserve of $4,850,000, the Origination Fee of $475,000, the Developer Fee of $2,835,000 and contingency of $1,440,000. Borrower shall not incur any cost in excess of the Approved Budget except as permitted under **Section 11.5** or funded by Equity Contributions.

## Section 11.2 Sources and Uses; Conforming of Budget

(a) As of the Effective Date, the sources of funds for the Project are (i) the Loan in the maximum amount of $47,500,000, (ii) the Mezzanine Loan in the amount of $9,200,000, and (iii) Equity Contributions in the amount of the Required Equity Contribution. Borrower acknowledges that the Approved Budget delivered with the draw schedule workbook dated January 8, 2025 allocates (A) the entire $8,200,000 land acquisition line item and $1,000,000 of the Developer Fee to proceeds of the Mezzanine Loan, and (B) $0 of land acquisition cost to Equity Contributions, and that the sources and uses statement in Section 5.1 of the Term Sheet reflects Equity Contributions of $0 and does not identify any source for the land acquisition cost.

(b) Borrower shall, on or before the Closing Date, deliver to Lender a conformed sources and uses statement (the "**Closing Statement**") that (i) identifies each source of funds and each use of funds, (ii) includes the Refinancing Payoff as a Project Cost (or demonstrates to Lender's satisfaction that the Prior Deed of Trust will be released without the use of Project funds), (iii) reflects the Required Equity Contribution and its verified source, (iv) demonstrates that sources equal uses, and (v) demonstrates compliance with **Section 2.4**. The Closing Statement approved by Lender shall be attached as **Schedule 11.2** and shall control for all purposes of this Agreement.

(c) Borrower acknowledges that Lender does not count the Mezzanine Loan as an Equity Contribution for any purpose, including the Loan-to-Cost Ratio, the Loan-to-Value Ratio, HVCRE contributed capital, or the minimum equity requirements of this Agreement.

## Section 11.3 Equity Requirement and Verification

Borrower shall deliver to Lender, not later than five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, (a) a source-of-funds certification executed by each member of Borrower contributing equity, (b) bank or brokerage statements evidencing the availability of the Required Equity Contribution, (c) wire instructions for the Equity Escrow Account, and (d) such other evidence as Lender may reasonably require to confirm that the Required Equity Contribution is not derived, directly or indirectly, from the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any of their respective Affiliates. Borrower's failure to deliver such evidence shall entitle Lender to decline to close.

## Section 11.4 Use of Equity

Equity Contributions shall be applied only to Project Costs and only in the order and manner described in **Section 9.8**. No Equity Contribution may be returned, refunded or distributed to any member of Borrower prior to the payment in full of the Obligations.

## Section 11.5 Reallocations; Contingency

Borrower may reallocate amounts among line items of the Approved Budget without Lender's consent only if (a) the reallocation is between line items within the same category (hard costs, soft costs or contingency), (b) no line item is increased or decreased by more than ten percent (10%) of its original amount and by not more than $250,000, (c) the reallocation does not reduce any hard cost line item below the amount required to complete the corresponding work, (d) the reallocation does not reduce the contingency below $500,000, and (e) Borrower delivers written notice of the reallocation to Lender within ten (10) Business Days. All other reallocations require Lender's prior written consent. The contingency shall be available to fund Approved Change Orders and documented cost overruns, in each case at Lender's discretion.

## Section 11.6 Developer Fee

The Developer Fee shall be funded from Loan proceeds only as and to the extent set forth in the Draw Schedule, and only if (a) no Default or Event of Default exists or would result therefrom, (b) the remaining undisbursed Loan proceeds, Retainage, contingency and committed Equity Contributions are sufficient to complete the Project in accordance with the Approved Budget, and (c) all hard costs and soft costs then due have been paid. The final portion of the Developer Fee reflected in Draw 9 shall be payable only upon satisfaction of the conditions to the release of Retainage under **Section 9.3(b)**. No Developer Fee shall be payable at any time during which a Construction Delay Default or an unremedied Interest Reserve Shortfall exists. Borrower acknowledges that the Developer Fee is not an Equity Contribution and shall not be credited toward any Financial Covenant.

## Section 11.7 HVCRE

Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Loan is expected to be classified as an HVCRE exposure, (b) the contributed capital of Borrower (consisting of the land contribution, if and to the extent properly counted as contributed capital, plus the Required Equity Contribution) is projected to equal approximately $10,340,000, or 14.2% of the $72,800,000 As-Completed Value, which is below the fifteen percent (15%) threshold, and (c) Lender would require contributed capital of not less than $10,920,000 to avoid HVCRE classification. Borrower shall cooperate with Lender in making any determination under the HVCRE rule, including by delivering documentation of the source, amount and timing of all contributions, and shall not take any position inconsistent with Lender's HVCRE classification for regulatory capital purposes.

# ARTICLE 12 — COLLATERAL; TITLE; SURVEY

## Section 12.1 Security

The Obligations shall be secured by: (a) a first priority Deed of Trust, Assignment of Rents, Security Agreement and Fixture Filing encumbering the Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions; (b) a first priority Assignment of Rents and Leases; (c) a first priority security interest in all personal property, fixtures, equipment, permits, plans, specifications, contracts, licenses, approvals, accounts and general intangibles relating to the Project, perfected by UCC-1 financing statements filed with the North Carolina Secretary of State and, as to fixtures, in the Durham County Registry; (d) the Assignments of Development Documents; (e) the Collateral Assignment of Insurance Proceeds and Condemnation Awards; (f) the Pledge Agreements pledging one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Borrower, subject to the lien subordination provisions of the Intercreditor Agreement; (g) the Pledged Account Agreements; and (h) such other collateral as Lender may reasonably require.

## Section 12.2 Priority of Membership Interest Pledge

Borrower acknowledges that the Mezzanine Loan is currently secured by a pledge of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Borrower, that Lender requires a first priority pledge of the same collateral, and that the resolution of such competing pledges is a condition to Closing. Borrower shall cause each of its members to execute and deliver the Pledge Agreements and shall cause the Mezzanine Lender to execute and deliver the Intercreditor Agreement providing that Lender's pledge is a first priority lien and the Mezzanine Lender's pledge is a second priority lien. Borrower shall cause each member to execute a consent to the pledge, cooperation in any UCC-8 filing, and an irrevocable proxy in favor of Lender exercisable during the continuance of an Event of Default, all in form satisfactory to Lender.

## Section 12.3 Title Policy

At Closing, Lender shall have received the Title Policy, issued by the Disbursement Agent, in an amount not less than the Commitment, insuring the Deed of Trust as a valid first priority lien on the Property subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, with such endorsements as Lender may require, including (a) access, (b) contiguity, (c) survey, (d) comprehensive, (e) zoning (3.0 with parking and loading), (f) subdivision, (g) location, (h) doing business, and (i) such additional endorsements as Lender may reasonably require. The Title Policy shall not contain any exception for the Prior Deed of Trust, any mechanics' or materialmen's lien arising from work performed prior to Closing, the Declaration of Land Use Restrictions required by the NFA Letter (other than as approved by Lender), or any other monetary lien.

## Section 12.4 Refinancing Payoff of Prior Deed of Trust

(a) Borrower shall cause the Prior Deed of Trust to be satisfied and released of record on the Closing Date concurrently with the recording of the Deed of Trust, and the Title Policy shall insure Lender's first priority lien free of the Prior Deed of Trust.

(b) Borrower shall deliver to Lender and the Disbursement Agent, not later than five (5) Business Days prior to Closing, a payoff letter from Triangle Commercial Bank (or its successor or assign), dated not more than thirty (30) days prior to Closing, stating the outstanding principal balance, all accrued and unpaid interest, per diem interest, fees, prepayment premiums, and the aggregate amount required to satisfy the indebtedness in full, together with (i) an executed cancellation of deed of trust or certificate of satisfaction in recordable form under N.C.G.S. §45-37, or (ii) the Disbursement Agent's undertaking to record a satisfaction upon disbursement of the Refinancing Payoff through escrow.

(c) Borrower acknowledges that the Title Commitment reflects that the Prior Deed of Trust secured an original indebtedness of $3,400,000 and that, according to the Title Commitment, Borrower's counsel has advised the Disbursement Agent that the indebtedness has been partially repaid and that the Company has not independently verified the outstanding balance. Borrower shall identify the source of the Refinancing Payoff on the Closing Statement, and such source shall not include the Mezzanine Loan or any source described in **Section 2.4(b)**.

## Section 12.5 Survey

Not later than ten (10) days prior to Closing, Borrower shall deliver to Lender and the Disbursement Agent the ALTA/NSPS Survey of the Property, prepared by a surveyor licensed in North Carolina, certified to Lender, Borrower and the Disbursement Agent, dated or re-certified within ninety (90) days of Closing, conforming to the 2021 ALTA/NSPS Minimum Standard Detail Requirements, and including Table A optional items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7(a), 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 as requested by Lender. The Survey shall (a) confirm the acreage and boundaries of each parcel and of the combined site, (b) depict the Affected Area, the Duke Energy utility easement, the stormwater management easement, the CC&Rs, and all other matters of record, (c) identify all improvements, encroachments and means of access, and (d) enable the deletion of the standard survey exceptions from the Title Policy.

## Section 12.6 Mechanics' Lien Priority; Pre-Closing Work

(a) Borrower acknowledges that under N.C.G.S. §44A-10 a claim of lien for labor or materials relates back to and is effective from the date of first furnishing of labor or materials at the site of the improvement, and that demolition, environmental remediation, rough grading, utility stubbing and other site work were performed on the Property in 2024 prior to the Closing Date. Accordingly, the Deed of Trust, when recorded, may be subject to claims of lien for such pre-Closing work unless the matters described in this Section are satisfied.

(b) As a condition to Closing, Borrower shall deliver to Lender (i) final, unconditional lien waivers and releases, in statutory form, from the Contractor, all demolition contractors, the environmental remediation contractor (Sentinel Environmental Consulting LLC or its subcontractors), the grading and site-work contractors and all materialmen that furnished labor or materials to the Property before the Closing Date; (ii) an owner's and contractor's affidavit in the form required by N.C.G.S. §44A-23 and satisfactory to the Disbursement Agent; and (iii) either (A) an unconditional mechanics' lien endorsement to the Title Policy (an ALTA 31 form or equivalent) or (B) such other affirmative coverage or indemnity from the Disbursement Agent as Lender may approve in writing. If Lender does not receive the items described in clauses (i) through (iii), Lender may decline to close.

(c) Borrower shall not permit any work to commence at the site prior to the recording of the Deed of Trust other than the work described in this Section for which waivers have been delivered.

## Section 12.7 Further Assurances

Borrower shall execute, deliver, file and record all such further instruments, financing statements, continuation statements, affidavits, certificates and other documents, and shall take all such further actions, as Lender may reasonably request to create, perfect, maintain and protect its Liens on the Property and the other collateral and to carry out the purposes of this Agreement.

## Section 12.8 Release of Collateral

Upon payment in full of the Obligations (including all amounts payable under the Guaranties and the Environmental Indemnity, which shall survive), and upon performance of all other obligations of Borrower under the Loan Documents, Lender shall execute and deliver to Borrower, at Borrower's expense, releases of the Deed of Trust, the Pledge Agreements and the other security instruments, and shall deliver to Borrower the pledged membership interests and any amounts remaining in the Interest Reserve Account, the Equity Escrow Account or any other pledged account.

# ARTICLE 13 — GUARANTIES

## Section 13.1 Completion Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several completion guaranty (the "**Completion Guaranty**") pursuant to which the Guarantors shall absolutely and unconditionally guarantee to Lender (a) the lien-free completion of the Project in accordance with the Plans and Specifications, the GMP Contract, the Approved Budget and the construction schedule, on or before the Outside Completion Date; (b) the funding of all costs of such completion in excess of the Loan proceeds, Retainage, contingency and Equity Contributions, without regard to any cost overrun, change order, casualty, Defect, contractor default, Insolvency Event affecting the Contractor or the Architect, or any other circumstance; and (c) payment of all amounts necessary to obtain the final, unconditional certificate of occupancy and to discharge all Liens (other than Permitted Exceptions). The Completion Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect until Lender has received evidence satisfactory to it that Final Completion has occurred. The Completion Guaranty is not limited in amount.

## Section 13.2 Carry Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several carry guaranty (the "**Carry Guaranty**") pursuant to which the Guarantors shall guarantee the payment of interest and all other carrying costs on the Loan during the term of the Loan, including (a) monthly interest, (b) real estate taxes and assessments, (c) insurance premiums, (d) the costs of completing the Project, (e) the reasonable costs of maintaining and operating the Property during any period of suspension or after an Event of Default, and (f) all Interest Reserve Shortfalls funded by Lender. The Carry Guaranty is in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Interest Reserve and shall apply to interest and carrying costs accruing after the Interest Reserve is exhausted or to the extent the Interest Reserve is insufficient.

## Section 13.3 Partial Repayment Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several partial repayment guaranty (the "**Partial Repayment Guaranty**") in the maximum aggregate amount of $11,875,000, being twenty-five percent (25%) of the original principal amount of the Loan (the "**Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount**"). The Partial Repayment Guaranty is a guarantee of payment and not of collection. The Guarantors shall be jointly and severally liable for the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount, meaning that each Guarantor is individually liable for the full Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount (and not merely for a pro rata share), **provided** that Lender shall not be entitled to recover more than the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount in the aggregate from all Guarantors under the Partial Repayment Guaranty. The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall become due and payable upon (a) the occurrence of an Event of Default and acceleration of the Loan, (b) the commencement of any foreclosure or other enforcement proceeding, or (c) the Maturity Date, whichever first occurs.

## Section 13.4 Recourse Triggers

Notwithstanding **Section 13.3**, the liability of the Guarantors under the Partial Repayment Guaranty shall become full recourse for the entire amount of the Obligations (and not merely the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount), less any amounts recovered by Lender from the realization on the collateral, upon the occurrence of any of the following (each, a "**Recourse Trigger**"): (a) fraud, intentional misrepresentation or willful misconduct by Borrower, any Guarantor, any member of Borrower or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing in connection with the Loan or the Loan Documents; (b) the voluntary filing by Borrower of a petition under the Bankruptcy Code or any other insolvency proceeding, or the consent by Borrower to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, or the collusive or bad-faith failure by Borrower to contest an involuntary petition; (c) any prohibited transfer, encumbrance, pledge or hypothecation of the Property, any membership interest in Borrower or any other collateral in violation of this Agreement, or any transfer that results in a change of control of Borrower; (d) any breach of the SPE covenants in **Article 18** or of the covenant to maintain the Independent Manager; (e) any Environmental Violation, any release of Hazardous Materials caused or permitted by Borrower, its agents or contractors, or any failure to comply with the NFA Letter, the Soil Management Plan or the Environmental Laws; (f) waste, arson, intentional destruction of the Property, or misapplication of insurance proceeds, condemnation awards, rents or security deposits; (g) the failure to complete the Project or the abandonment of the Project; (h) the misapplication or diversion of Loan proceeds, including any use of proceeds in violation of **Section 2.2**; (i) any amendment, modification or refinancing of the Mezzanine Loan in violation of **Section 25.6** or the Intercreditor Agreement; and (j) Borrower's assertion in any proceeding that any Loan Document is unenforceable or that the Loan is nonrecourse. Lender may pursue the Guarantors for the full amount of the Obligations upon the occurrence of a Recourse Trigger, and the Guarantors shall not be entitled to any reduction for the value of the collateral or for any nonrecourse limitation contained in any Loan Document.

## Section 13.5 Environmental Indemnity

Each Guarantor, and Borrower, shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, an environmental indemnity agreement (the "**Environmental Indemnity**") in form satisfactory to Lender, pursuant to which Borrower and the Guarantors shall, jointly and severally, indemnify and hold harmless Lender and the other Indemnified Parties from and against all losses, liabilities, claims, damages, penalties, fines, judgments, remediation costs, natural resource damages, diminution in value, consultants' fees and attorneys' fees arising out of or relating to (a) the presence, release, threatened release or migration of Hazardous Materials at, on, under, from or migrating to or from the Property, including the residual petroleum contamination described in the Phase I ESA and the NFA Letter; (b) any violation of or liability under any Environmental Law relating to the Property; (c) any failure to comply with the NFA Letter, the Soil Management Plan or the Deed Notice; (d) the breach of any representation, warranty or covenant in **Article 19**; and (e) any claim by any Governmental Authority or third party relating to any of the foregoing. The Environmental Indemnity shall be unlimited in amount and shall survive repayment of the Loan, the release or reconveyance of the Deed of Trust, and any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure or acceptance of a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.

## Section 13.6 Guarantor Waivers

# ARTICLE 16 — FINANCIAL COVENANTS

## Section 16.1 Loan-to-Value Ratio

The LTV shall not exceed sixty-five percent (65%) at any time, tested (a) at Closing, (b) at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period, (c) upon any reappraisal under **Section 16.9**, and (d) annually thereafter. Borrower acknowledges that the LTV as of the Effective Date, based on the Appraisal, is 65.25% on an as-completed basis ($47,500,000 ÷ $72,800,000) and 62.34% on an as-stabilized basis ($47,500,000 ÷ $76,200,000), and that the as-completed LTV exceeds the 65% limit by approximately $180,000 of principal. At or before Closing, Borrower shall either (i) reduce the principal amount of the Loan by $180,000, or (ii) deposit additional Equity Contributions in an amount sufficient to reduce the Loan-to-Value Ratio to not more than 65%, or (iii) deliver a reappraisal satisfactory to Lender demonstrating compliance.

## Section 16.2 Loan-to-Cost Ratio

The LTC shall not exceed eighty percent (80%) at any time, tested at Closing and at each Advance with reference to Total Project Costs as then reflected in the Approved Budget. Borrower acknowledges that, without giving effect to the Required Equity Contribution and the conforming of the Approved Budget under **Section 11.2**, the LTC is 83.77% ($47,500,000 ÷ $56,700,000).

## Section 16.3 Minimum DSCR

(a) **Test.** The DSCR shall not be less than 1.25x, tested (i) at the commencement of the Mini-Perm Period, calculated on a pro forma basis using Stabilized NOI and Senior Debt Service (and not on the basis of actual trailing twelve-month net operating income, which the parties acknowledge will not be meaningful until the Project has been operating and leasing for a reasonable period), (ii) at the first anniversary of Substantial Completion, (iii) annually thereafter, and (iv) upon any reappraisal under **Section 16.9**.

(b) **Cure.** If the DSCR is less than 1.25x at any test date, Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days after written notice from Lender, at Lender's election either (i) prepay the Loan in an amount sufficient to restore the DSCR to not less than 1.25x, or (ii) deposit cash collateral with Lender in an amount determined by Lender to be sufficient to restore the DSCR to not less than 1.25x, to be held in a pledged account and applied to the Obligations in accordance with Lender's instructions. Borrower's failure to cure within such period shall constitute an Event of Default under **Section 24.3**.

## Section 16.4 Combined Debt Service Coverage

(a) **Test.** From and after the first anniversary of Substantial Completion, the Combined DSCR shall not be less than 1.10x, tested annually. Borrower acknowledges that, based on Stabilized NOI of $4,876,800, Senior Debt Service of $3,728,750 (interest only at 7.85%) and Mezzanine Debt Service of approximately $1,150,000 per annum (12.50% on a $9,200,000 balance, before giving effect to paid-in-kind accrual), the Combined DSCR as of the Effective Date would be approximately 1.00x, and that, giving effect to the accrual of paid-in-kind interest on the Mezzanine Loan during the Construction Period (which would increase the Mezzanine Loan balance to approximately $12,075,000 by the Construction Maturity Date on a simple-interest basis), the Combined DSCR would be approximately 0.93x. The parties acknowledge that the Financial Covenants and the take-out strategy depend upon (i) the Mezzanine Lender's agreement to defer or capitalize a substantial portion of its interest, (ii) achievement of NOI in excess of the Appraisal's projection, or (iii) repayment or restructuring of the Mezzanine Loan at or before the Mini-Perm Period, and Borrower shall deliver to Lender, as a condition to conversion to the Mini-Perm Period, evidence reasonably satisfactory to Lender that the Combined DSCR will be satisfied or that the Mezzanine Loan will be repaid or restructured.

(b) **Cure.** If the Combined DSCR is less than 1.10x, Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days after notice, either (i) cause the Mezzanine Loan to be repaid, reduced or restructured so as to restore compliance, (ii) prepay the Loan in an amount sufficient to restore compliance, or (iii) deposit cash collateral with Lender in an amount sufficient to restore compliance.

# ARTICLE 18 — SINGLE-PURPOSE ENTITY; SEPARATENESS; INDEPENDENT MANAGER

## Section 18.1 SPE Covenants

Borrower shall at all times maintain its status as a single-purpose, bankruptcy-remote entity and shall:

(a) hold no assets other than the Property, the Project and related assets (including cash and cash equivalents and the accounts contemplated by the Loan Documents);

(b) incur no liabilities other than the Permitted Indebtedness, the Loan Documents, and trade payables and accrued expenses incurred in the ordinary course of business;

(c) conduct no business other than the ownership, development, construction, leasing, management and operation of the Project;

(d) maintain its own books, records, financial statements, bank accounts and payroll separate from those of any member, Affiliate or other Person, and not commingle its funds or other assets with those of any member, Affiliate or other Person;

(e) hold itself out as a separate and distinct entity, conduct its business in its own name, and not hold itself out as being liable for the debts of any member or Affiliate or as a division or part of any other Person;

(f) observe all organizational formalities, maintain minutes and records of member and manager actions, and make all required filings with the North Carolina Secretary of State;

(g) pay its own liabilities and expenses from its own funds, and allocate shared overhead and shared expenses (if any) on a basis that is fair and reasonable and that reflects arm's-length dealings;

(h) maintain arm's-length relationships with all Affiliates and enter into no transaction with an Affiliate except on arm's-length terms documented in writing;

(i) not guarantee or become obligated for the debts of any other Person, and not pledge its assets for the benefit of any other Person;

(j) not acquire obligations or securities of any member or Affiliate, and not make any loans to any member or Affiliate;

(k) not identify any member or Affiliate as a division or part of Borrower, and correct any known misunderstanding regarding its separate identity;

(l) maintain adequate capital in light of its contemplated business operations, and cause its members to make the capital contributions required by the Operating Agreement and the Approved Budget;

(m) not commingle any funds held in trust or otherwise for the benefit of third parties;

(n) not engage in any transaction with the Mezzanine Lender except as permitted by the Mezzanine Loan documents and the Intercreditor Agreement; and

(o) file its own tax returns and not file a consolidated return with any member or Affiliate.

## Section 18.2 Independent Manager

(a) **Requirement.** As a condition to Closing, Borrower's Operating Agreement shall be amended to provide, and Borrower shall at all times maintain, at least one manager (the "**Independent Manager**") who (i) is not, and has not been within the preceding five (5) years, an officer, director, manager, employee, member, creditor, supplier, customer, attorney, accountant or Affiliate of Borrower, any member of Borrower, the Mezzanine Lender, Thomas R. Chen or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing; (ii) has no economic interest in Borrower or any such Person; and (iii) is provided by a nationally recognized independent director/manager service provider acceptable to Lender (or is otherwise acceptable to Lender in its reasonable discretion).

(b) **Authority.** The affirmative vote of the Independent Manager shall be required for Borrower to (i) file a voluntary petition under the Bankruptcy Code or consent to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, (ii) make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, (iii) admit in writing its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due, (iv) dissolve, liquidate, merge, consolidate or transfer all or substantially all of its assets, or (v) amend the provisions of the Operating Agreement relating to the Independent Manager.

(c) **Removal.** The Independent Manager may not be removed, and the provisions of the Operating Agreement relating to the Independent Manager may not be amended, without Lender's prior written consent.

(d) **Springing Obligation.** If at any time Borrower's Operating Agreement does not contain the provisions required by this Section, Borrower shall, within ten (10) Business Days after notice from Lender, cause such provisions to be adopted and an Independent Manager to be appointed.

(e) **Costs.** Borrower shall pay all reasonable costs and fees of the Independent Manager and the service provider.

## Section 18.3 Non-Consolidation Opinion

As a condition to Closing, Borrower's counsel (Calloway & Strauss PLLC) shall deliver to Lender a substantive non-consolidation opinion (the "**Non-Consolidation Opinion**"), in form and substance satisfactory to Lender and its counsel, opining that, subject to customary assumptions and qualifications, a court applying applicable North Carolina law (with such reference to Delaware limited liability company law as counsel deems appropriate) would not substantively consolidate the assets and liabilities of Borrower with those of any member of Borrower, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen or any other Affiliate of Borrower in any bankruptcy or insolvency proceeding of Borrower or any such Person. The Non-Consolidation Opinion shall be updated, if requested by Lender, in connection with any material amendment to the Operating Agreement or the Mezzanine Loan, or upon any change in the organizational structure of Borrower.

## Section 18.4 Affiliate Relationship; Acknowledgment

Borrower acknowledges and discloses to Lender that Thomas R. Chen is the managing member of both Brightleaf Investors Group LLC (which holds a 28% membership interest in Borrower) and Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC (the Mezzanine Lender), and that Brightleaf Investors Group LLC received its membership interest in Borrower in consideration of its commitment to arrange the mezzanine financing for the Project rather than for a cash capital contribution. Borrower shall ensure that the Intercreditor Agreement includes express acknowledgments of this relationship and provisions prohibiting the Mezzanine Lender from using its affiliate relationship to the detriment of Lender. Borrower shall promptly notify Lender of any change in the ownership or control of Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Brightleaf Mezzanine Capital LLC or Borrower.

## Section 18.5 Member Approval; Consents

Borrower represents that, as of the Closing Date, (a) the execution, delivery and performance of the Loan Documents, (b) the grant of the Pledge Agreements, (c) the amendments to the Operating Agreement required by this Article, and (d) the grant of the irrevocable proxies required by **Section 12.2**, have each been approved by the members of Borrower as required by Section 3.2 and Section 9.1 of the Operating Agreement, and that all such approvals remain in full force and effect. Borrower shall deliver to Lender certified copies of all such member consents and the executed amendment to the Operating Agreement.

## Section 18.6 Breach a Recourse Trigger

Any breach of this Article shall constitute an Event of Default and a Recourse Trigger under **Section 13.4(d)**.

# ARTICLE 19 — ENVIRONMENTAL COVENANTS

## Section 19.1 Compliance with Environmental Laws

Borrower shall, and shall cause all contractors, subcontractors, tenants and occupants to, comply with all Environmental Laws and with all permits, licenses and approvals relating to the environmental condition of the Property. Borrower shall not cause or permit any Release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under or from the Property, and shall not use the Property for any use that would cause Lender to be deemed an "owner or operator" under CERCLA or any similar state law.

## Section 19.2 NFA Letter Compliance

Borrower shall comply with each condition of the NFA Letter and shall, in particular:

(a) **Condition 1 — Vapor Mitigation System.** Cause the Vapor Mitigation System to be designed by a professional engineer licensed in North Carolina, incorporated into the Plans and Specifications, installed beneath any enclosed structure constructed over the Affected Area in accordance with the NCDEQ Division of Waste Management guidelines for vapor intrusion mitigation, and made capable of conversion from passive to active depressurization. Borrower shall deliver as-built drawings and a system performance verification report to NCDEQ within ninety (90) days after completion of the building foundation in the Affected Area, and shall deliver copies of all such submissions and any NCDEQ response to Lender within five (5) Business Days after submission or receipt. Borrower shall maintain the Vapor Mitigation System in good working order for so long as the NFA Letter remains in effect and shall not decommission, modify or impair the system without Lender's prior written consent.

(b) **Condition 2 — Non-Residential Land Use Restriction.** Not construct, use, lease, occupy or permit the occupancy of any residential dwelling unit, or any other "residential use" within the meaning of the NFA Letter, within the Affected Area, unless and until Borrower has obtained from NCDEQ a written modification of the NFA Letter expressly permitting such use, in form and substance satisfactory to Lender, and has delivered a copy thereof to Lender together with an updated appraisal and such other information as Lender may require. Borrower acknowledges that Lender's underwriting and the Appraisal do not reflect the loss of any residential units, and that if the NFA Letter is not modified, Borrower must (i) redesign the Affected Area units (or the affected portion of the building) as non-residential space and deliver revised Plans and Specifications and revised income projections, and (ii) demonstrate to Lender's satisfaction that the Financial Covenants are satisfied on the revised program.

(c) **Condition 3 — Soil Management Plan.** Prior to any excavation, grading or other subsurface disturbance in the Affected Area, prepare and submit to NCDEQ for approval, and obtain NCDEQ's approval of, the Soil Management Plan addressing soil screening, stockpile management, dust control, worker health and safety, personal protective equipment, disposal of impacted soil and confirmation sampling. Borrower shall incorporate the Soil Management Plan into the construction documents, deliver a copy to the Contractor and all relevant subcontractors, provide training to all site personnel, and deliver a copy of the approved Soil Management Plan to Lender.

(d) **Condition 4 — Deed Notice.** Cause the Deed Notice to be prepared, executed and recorded in the Durham County Registry of Deeds in accordance with the NFA Letter, and deliver to Lender a certified copy of the recorded Deed Notice with the recording stamp. Borrower acknowledges that the NFA Letter required the Deed Notice to be recorded within sixty (60) days after September 30, 2024 (i.e., on or before November 29, 2024), that the Phase I ESA dated October 28, 2024 does not reflect that the Deed Notice had been recorded, and that the Deed Notice is not reflected in the Title Commitment. Borrower shall deliver evidence of the recorded Deed Notice not later than five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, or, if not previously recorded, shall cause it to be recorded on the Closing Date concurrently with the recording of the Deed of Trust, and shall deliver to Lender a written statement from NCDEQ or environmental counsel confirming that the late recording does not impair the NFA determination.

## Section 19.3 Environmental Reporting

Borrower shall deliver to Lender (a) copies of all submissions to and correspondence with NCDEQ relating to the Property, within five (5) Business Days after submission or receipt; (b) evidence of the annual inspection and certification of the Vapor Mitigation System within thirty (30) days after completion; (c) copies of all indoor air quality or sub-slab soil gas monitoring results, within ten (10) days after receipt; and (d) an annual environmental compliance certificate, signed by the Managing Member, certifying compliance with this Article and the NFA Letter.

## Section 19.4 No Further Remediation; Additional Investigation

If any Governmental Authority requires additional investigation, remediation, monitoring or reporting with respect to the Property, or if Lender reasonably determines that any Hazardous Materials condition at the Property requires investigation or remediation, Borrower shall, at its sole cost, promptly undertake and diligently complete such work in accordance with applicable Environmental Laws and shall keep Lender fully informed. Borrower shall not enter into any consent decree, administrative order or settlement relating to the environmental condition of the Property without Lender's prior written consent.

## Section 19.5 Notice of Releases

Borrower shall notify Lender in writing within twenty-four (24) hours after Borrower obtains knowledge of (a) any Release or threatened Release of Hazardous Materials at, on, under or from the Property that requires reporting under any Environmental Law, (b) any inspection, investigation, notice of violation, order or information request from any Governmental Authority relating to the environmental condition of the Property, or (c) any claim by any third party relating to Hazardous Materials or Environmental Laws.

## Section 19.6 Lender's Environmental Rights

Lender may, at Borrower's expense (but not more than once per year in the absence of an Event of Default or a reasonable basis for concern), obtain a Phase I ESA update or other environmental assessment of the Property. Borrower shall cooperate with any such assessment and shall provide access to the Property and to all environmental records. Borrower shall not communicate with NCDEQ regarding the NFA Letter, the Affected Area or the Vapor Mitigation System without prior notice to Lender (except in an emergency), and shall permit Lender's counsel to participate in any such communications.

## Section 19.7 Environmental Indemnity; Survival

The Environmental Indemnity shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, the covenants in this Article, and shall survive repayment of the Loan and any transfer of the Property by foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure or otherwise. The obligations of Borrower and the Guarantors under this Article and the Environmental Indemnity shall not be limited by any exculpatory or nonrecourse provision of any Loan Document.

## Section 19.8 Pollution Legal Liability Insurance

Lender may require, and Borrower shall obtain within sixty (60) days after Lender's written request, a pollution legal liability insurance policy (or environmental remediation insurance) with coverage, limits, deductible, term and insurer rating reasonably satisfactory to Lender, naming Lender as additional insured and loss payee, and shall collaterally assign such policy to Lender. Lender's failure to require such insurance at Closing shall not constitute a waiver of its right to require it thereafter.

## Section 19.9 Environmental Default

Any failure to comply with this Article, the NFA Letter, the Soil Management Plan or the Deed Notice shall constitute an Event of Default under **Section 24.13** and a Recourse Trigger under **Section 13.4(e)**.

## Section 19.10 Lender Not an Operator

Nothing in this Agreement, and no inspection, approval, consent or advance by Lender, shall be deemed to make Lender an "owner or operator," "arranger," "transporter" or "participant in management" of the Property or the Project for purposes of CERCLA, any Environmental Law or any other law. Borrower shall include in all leases and construction contracts such provisions as are reasonably necessary to preserve Lender's secured creditor exemption.

# ARTICLE 10 — CONSTRUCTION COVENANTS

## Section 10.1 Commencement and Continuity of Construction

Borrower shall cause construction of the Project to commence not later than thirty (30) days after the Closing Date and to be prosecuted diligently and continuously, in a good and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the Plans and Specifications, the GMP Contract, the Approved Budget, all applicable permits and Legal Requirements, and the approved construction schedule. Borrower shall not suspend or abandon construction for more than fifteen (15) consecutive days (other than as a result of an Unavoidable Delay that is not caused by Borrower, the Contractor or any Affiliate of either, and as to which Borrower has delivered prior written notice to Lender).

## Section 10.2 Plans and Specifications

Lender has reviewed and approved the Plans and Specifications identified in **Schedule 10.2** for purposes of this Agreement only. Borrower shall not modify the Plans and Specifications in any material respect, and shall not permit any material deviation from the Plans and Specifications, without Lender's prior written consent. For purposes of this Section, a modification is "material" if it (a) changes the number or mix of residential units or the amount of retail square footage; (b) changes the building footprint, height, structural system, exterior materials or parking count; (c) relocates any residential occupancy space into or above the Affected Area; (d) changes the scope or design of the Vapor Mitigation System; (e) would require any rezoning, variance, special use permit or other discretionary approval; (f) would require any additional approval of the Brightleaf Historic District Association Architectural Review Committee; or (g) increases hard costs by more than $500,000 in the aggregate.

## Section 10.3 GMP Contract; Change Orders

(a) Borrower shall not amend, modify, terminate, replace or assign the GMP Contract (other than the collateral assignment to Lender) without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall cause the Contractor to perform in accordance with the GMP Contract, and shall enforce the GMP Contract for the benefit of Lender.

(b) Borrower may approve individual change orders that, in the aggregate with all other change orders, do not exceed $250,000 and do not constitute a material modification under **Section 10.2** without Lender's consent, provided that (i) such change orders are funded from the contingency line item of the Approved Budget or from Equity Contributions, (ii) Borrower delivers a copy of each such change order to Lender within ten (10) Business Days, and (iii) no such change order reduces the scope of the Project or the quality of the work. All other change orders require Lender's prior written consent ("**Approved Change Orders**").

(c) Borrower shall deliver to Lender, within ten (10) days after execution, a copy of each Approved Change Order, together with the Contractor's and Architect's certification of the resulting contract amount and schedule impact.

(d) Borrower shall not permit the aggregate of the GMP Contract amount plus all Approved Change Orders to exceed the hard cost line items of the Approved Budget unless the excess is funded from the contingency line item or from Equity Contributions deposited with Lender.

## Section 10.4 Contractor and Architect Requirements

(a) Borrower shall not terminate, replace or substitute the Contractor or the Architect without Lender's prior written consent. Any replacement contractor or architect must be approved by Lender and must satisfy the requirements of this Section.

(b) Borrower shall cause the Contractor to (i) maintain its North Carolina general contractor's license in good standing, (ii) maintain the insurance required under **Article 20** and the GMP Contract, (iii) deliver payment and performance bonds in the full amount of the GMP Contract (100%) from a surety acceptable to Lender and rated at least A- by A.M. Best, unless waived by Lender in writing, and (iv) deliver, within thirty (30) days after the Closing Date, its audited or reviewed financial statements for the two most recent fiscal years and a statement of bonding capacity. The requirement for payment and performance bonds shall be a condition to the first Progress Advance.

(c) Borrower shall cause the Architect to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per claim, and to deliver a collateral assignment of the Architect's Agreement, together with consents to assignment from the Contractor and the Architect.

## Section 10.5 Construction Schedule; Construction Delay Default

Borrower has delivered the baseline construction schedule approved by Lender (the "**Baseline Schedule**"), which reflects a Projected Substantial Completion Date of August 31, 2027. Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Construction Maturity Date of August 28, 2027 precedes the Projected Substantial Completion Date of August 31, 2027, and (b) accordingly the Loan contemplates that Substantial Completion may occur during the Mini-Perm Period. Borrower shall deliver an updated construction schedule with each monthly progress report. If at any time the Project is more than ninety (90) days behind the Baseline Schedule (as adjusted for Approved Change Orders and Unavoidable Delays), a Construction Delay Default shall exist under **Section 24.9**.

## Section 10.6 Compliance with Legal Requirements; Permits

Borrower shall comply, and shall cause the Contractor and the Architect to comply, with all Legal Requirements applicable to the Property, the Project and the construction, including all building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, energy, zoning, stormwater, sedimentation and Environmental Laws. Borrower shall obtain and maintain all permits, licenses, approvals and certificates required for the construction and occupancy of the Project, including the building permits, the certificates of occupancy, the Zoning Report, the right-of-way and utility approvals, and all approvals required under the Brightleaf Historic District Association Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions recorded in Book 6984, Page 1155, as amended by the First Amendment recorded in Book 7102, Page 388, Durham County Registry (the "**CC&Rs**").

## Section 10.7 Brightleaf Historic District Architectural Review

Borrower shall, as a condition to Closing and thereafter as a continuing covenant, (a) submit the final Plans and Specifications to the Brightleaf Historic District Association Architectural Review Committee in accordance with Article V of the CC&Rs, and (b) obtain the written approval of the Architectural Review Committee (or the lapse of the sixty (60) day deemed-approval period under Section 5 of the CC&Rs without written action). Borrower shall deliver evidence of such approval to Lender not later than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date. Borrower shall comply with the architectural review and design standards of the CC&Rs and with the assessment obligations thereunder, which Borrower acknowledges are currently assessed at $0.12 per square foot of gross building area per annum (approximately $34,500 per annum for the Project) and are not separately identified as a line item in the Appraisal's operating expense projection. Any modification to the Plans and Specifications requiring architectural review committee approval shall not be implemented until such approval is obtained.

## Section 10.8 Close-Out Deliverables

Upon Substantial Completion, and as a condition to the release of Retainage, Borrower shall deliver to Lender: (a) the final, unconditional certificate of occupancy for all residential units, retail bays and the parking garage; (b) the Architect's certificate of final completion; (c) as-built Plans and Specifications and CAD files; (d) all warranties, guaranties, operating manuals, attic stock and training materials, together with assignments of all contractor and manufacturer warranties; (e) final, unconditional lien waivers and releases from the Contractor, the Architect, all subcontractors and all materialmen; (f) an updated ALTA/NSPS Survey showing the Project as built, with no encroachments or survey defects other than those approved by Lender; (g) evidence that all punchlist items have been completed; (h) evidence of final inspection sign-off by the City of Durham and the fire marshal; (i) evidence of compliance with the life-safety, accessibility and energy-code requirements; and (j) such other close-out items as Lender may reasonably require.

## Section 10.9 Leasing and Stabilization

From and after Substantial Completion, Borrower shall use commercially reasonable efforts to lease the Project to Stabilization, shall lease the Property in accordance with the Approved Leasing Guidelines (as approved by Lender prior to the first lease), and shall not enter into any lease of more than 5,000 square feet of retail space, any lease with a term (including options) exceeding fifteen (15) years, any lease requiring landlord construction work in excess of $250,000, or any lease that is not on arm's-length terms without Lender's prior written consent. Borrower shall deliver the Rent Roll and a leasing status report with each quarterly report delivered under **Article 23**.

## Section 10.10 Defects; Corrective Work

Borrower shall promptly correct, or cause the Contractor to correct, any Defect in the Project. If Borrower fails to do so within thirty (30) days after notice from Lender (or such longer period as is reasonably necessary provided Borrower is diligently pursuing cure), Lender may perform such work as a protective advance under **Section 9.10**, and the cost thereof shall be an Obligation.

# ARTICLE 11 — APPROVED BUDGET; SOURCES AND USES; EQUITY

## Section 11.1 Approved Budget

The Approved Budget is attached as **Exhibit B** and reflects Total Project Costs of $56,700,000, comprising land acquisition of $8,200,000, hard construction costs of $34,750,000, soft costs of $4,150,000, the Interest Reserve of $4,850,000, the Origination Fee of $475,000, the Developer Fee of $2,835,000 and contingency of $1,440,000. Borrower shall not incur any cost in excess of the Approved Budget except as permitted under **Section 11.5** or funded by Equity Contributions.

## Section 11.2 Sources and Uses; Conforming of Budget

(a) As of the Effective Date, the sources of funds for the Project are (i) the Loan in the maximum amount of $47,500,000, (ii) the Mezzanine Loan in the amount of $9,200,000, and (iii) Equity Contributions in the amount of the Required Equity Contribution. Borrower acknowledges that the Approved Budget delivered with the draw schedule workbook dated January 8, 2025 allocates (A) the entire $8,200,000 land acquisition line item and $1,000,000 of the Developer Fee to proceeds of the Mezzanine Loan, and (B) $0 of land acquisition cost to Equity Contributions, and that the sources and uses statement in Section 5.1 of the Term Sheet reflects Equity Contributions of $0 and does not identify any source for the land acquisition cost.

(b) Borrower shall, on or before the Closing Date, deliver to Lender a conformed sources and uses statement (the "**Closing Statement**") that (i) identifies each source of funds and each use of funds, (ii) includes the Refinancing Payoff as a Project Cost (or demonstrates to Lender's satisfaction that the Prior Deed of Trust will be released without the use of Project funds), (iii) reflects the Required Equity Contribution and its verified source, (iv) demonstrates that sources equal uses, and (v) demonstrates compliance with **Section 2.4**. The Closing Statement approved by Lender shall be attached as **Schedule 11.2** and shall control for all purposes of this Agreement.

(c) Borrower acknowledges that Lender does not count the Mezzanine Loan as an Equity Contribution for any purpose, including the Loan-to-Cost Ratio, the Loan-to-Value Ratio, HVCRE contributed capital, or the minimum equity requirements of this Agreement.

## Section 11.3 Equity Requirement and Verification

Borrower shall deliver to Lender, not later than five (5) Business Days prior to the Closing Date, (a) a source-of-funds certification executed by each member of Borrower contributing equity, (b) bank or brokerage statements evidencing the availability of the Required Equity Contribution, (c) wire instructions for the Equity Escrow Account, and (d) such other evidence as Lender may reasonably require to confirm that the Required Equity Contribution is not derived, directly or indirectly, from the Mezzanine Loan, the Mezzanine Lender, Brightleaf Investors Group LLC, Thomas R. Chen, or any of their respective Affiliates. Borrower's failure to deliver such evidence shall entitle Lender to decline to close.

## Section 11.4 Use of Equity

Equity Contributions shall be applied only to Project Costs and only in the order and manner described in **Section 9.8**. No Equity Contribution may be returned, refunded or distributed to any member of Borrower prior to the payment in full of the Obligations.

## Section 11.5 Reallocations; Contingency

Borrower may reallocate amounts among line items of the Approved Budget without Lender's consent only if (a) the reallocation is between line items within the same category (hard costs, soft costs or contingency), (b) no line item is increased or decreased by more than ten percent (10%) of its original amount and by not more than $250,000, (c) the reallocation does not reduce any hard cost line item below the amount required to complete the corresponding work, (d) the reallocation does not reduce the contingency below $500,000, and (e) Borrower delivers written notice of the reallocation to Lender within ten (10) Business Days. All other reallocations require Lender's prior written consent. The contingency shall be available to fund Approved Change Orders and documented cost overruns, in each case at Lender's discretion.

## Section 11.6 Developer Fee

The Developer Fee shall be funded from Loan proceeds only as and to the extent set forth in the Draw Schedule, and only if (a) no Default or Event of Default exists or would result therefrom, (b) the remaining undisbursed Loan proceeds, Retainage, contingency and committed Equity Contributions are sufficient to complete the Project in accordance with the Approved Budget, and (c) all hard costs and soft costs then due have been paid. The final portion of the Developer Fee reflected in Draw 9 shall be payable only upon satisfaction of the conditions to the release of Retainage under **Section 9.3(b)**. No Developer Fee shall be payable at any time during which a Construction Delay Default or an unremedied Interest Reserve Shortfall exists. Borrower acknowledges that the Developer Fee is not an Equity Contribution and shall not be credited toward any Financial Covenant.

## Section 11.7 HVCRE

Borrower acknowledges that (a) the Loan is expected to be classified as an HVCRE exposure, (b) the contributed capital of Borrower (consisting of the land contribution, if and to the extent properly counted as contributed capital, plus the Required Equity Contribution) is projected to equal approximately $10,340,000, or 14.2% of the $72,800,000 As-Completed Value, which is below the fifteen percent (15%) threshold, and (c) Lender would require contributed capital of not less than $10,920,000 to avoid HVCRE classification. Borrower shall cooperate with Lender in making any determination under the HVCRE rule, including by delivering documentation of the source, amount and timing of all contributions, and shall not take any position inconsistent with Lender's HVCRE classification for regulatory capital purposes.

# ARTICLE 12 — COLLATERAL; TITLE; SURVEY

## Section 12.1 Security

The Obligations shall be secured by: (a) a first priority Deed of Trust, Assignment of Rents, Security Agreement and Fixture Filing encumbering the Property, subject only to the Permitted Exceptions; (b) a first priority Assignment of Rents and Leases; (c) a first priority security interest in all personal property, fixtures, equipment, permits, plans, specifications, contracts, licenses, approvals, accounts and general intangibles relating to the Project, perfected by UCC-1 financing statements filed with the North Carolina Secretary of State and, as to fixtures, in the Durham County Registry; (d) the Assignments of Development Documents; (e) the Collateral Assignment of Insurance Proceeds and Condemnation Awards; (f) the Pledge Agreements pledging one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Borrower, subject to the lien subordination provisions of the Intercreditor Agreement; (g) the Pledged Account Agreements; and (h) such other collateral as Lender may reasonably require.

## Section 12.2 Priority of Membership Interest Pledge

Borrower acknowledges that the Mezzanine Loan is currently secured by a pledge of one hundred percent (100%) of the membership interests in Borrower, that Lender requires a first priority pledge of the same collateral, and that the resolution of such competing pledges is a condition to Closing. Borrower shall cause each of its members to execute and deliver the Pledge Agreements and shall cause the Mezzanine Lender to execute and deliver the Intercreditor Agreement providing that Lender's pledge is a first priority lien and the Mezzanine Lender's pledge is a second priority lien. Borrower shall cause each member to execute a consent to the pledge, cooperation in any UCC-8 filing, and an irrevocable proxy in favor of Lender exercisable during the continuance of an Event of Default, all in form satisfactory to Lender.

## Section 12.3 Title Policy

At Closing, Lender shall have received the Title Policy, issued by the Disbursement Agent, in an amount not less than the Commitment, insuring the Deed of Trust as a valid first priority lien on the Property subject only to the Permitted Exceptions, with such endorsements as Lender may require, including (a) access, (b) contiguity, (c) survey, (d) comprehensive, (e) zoning (3.0 with parking and loading), (f) subdivision, (g) location, (h) doing business, and (i) such additional endorsements as Lender may reasonably require. The Title Policy shall not contain any exception for the Prior Deed of Trust, any mechanics' or materialmen's lien arising from work performed prior to Closing, the Declaration of Land Use Restrictions required by the NFA Letter (other than as approved by Lender), or any other monetary lien.

## Section 12.4 Refinancing Payoff of Prior Deed of Trust

(a) Borrower shall cause the Prior Deed of Trust to be satisfied and released of record on the Closing Date concurrently with the recording of the Deed of Trust, and the Title Policy shall insure Lender's first priority lien free of the Prior Deed of Trust.

(b) Borrower shall deliver to Lender and the Disbursement Agent, not later than five (5) Business Days prior to Closing, a payoff letter from Triangle Commercial Bank (or its successor or assign), dated not more than thirty (30) days prior to Closing, stating the outstanding principal balance, all accrued and unpaid interest, per diem interest, fees, prepayment premiums, and the aggregate amount required to satisfy the indebtedness in full, together with (i) an executed cancellation of deed of trust or certificate of satisfaction in recordable form under N.C.G.S. §45-37, or (ii) the Disbursement Agent's undertaking to record a satisfaction upon disbursement of the Refinancing Payoff through escrow.

(c) Borrower acknowledges that the Title Commitment reflects that the Prior Deed of Trust secured an original indebtedness of $3,400,000 and that, according to the Title Commitment, Borrower's counsel has advised the Disbursement Agent that the indebtedness has been partially repaid and that the Company has not independently verified the outstanding balance. Borrower shall identify the source of the Refinancing Payoff on the Closing Statement, and such source shall not include the Mezzanine Loan or any source described in **Section 2.4(b)**.

## Section 12.5 Survey

Not later than ten (10) days prior to Closing, Borrower shall deliver to Lender and the Disbursement Agent the ALTA/NSPS Survey of the Property, prepared by a surveyor licensed in North Carolina, certified to Lender, Borrower and the Disbursement Agent, dated or re-certified within ninety (90) days of Closing, conforming to the 2021 ALTA/NSPS Minimum Standard Detail Requirements, and including Table A optional items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7(a), 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 as requested by Lender. The Survey shall (a) confirm the acreage and boundaries of each parcel and of the combined site, (b) depict the Affected Area, the Duke Energy utility easement, the stormwater management easement, the CC&Rs, and all other matters of record, (c) identify all improvements, encroachments and means of access, and (d) enable the deletion of the standard survey exceptions from the Title Policy.

## Section 12.6 Mechanics' Lien Priority; Pre-Closing Work

(a) Borrower acknowledges that under N.C.G.S. §44A-10 a claim of lien for labor or materials relates back to and is effective from the date of first furnishing of labor or materials at the site of the improvement, and that demolition, environmental remediation, rough grading, utility stubbing and other site work were performed on the Property in 2024 prior to the Closing Date. # ARTICLE 13 — GUARANTIES

## Section 13.1 Completion Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several completion guaranty (the "**Completion Guaranty**") pursuant to which the Guarantors shall absolutely and unconditionally guarantee to Lender (a) the lien-free completion of the Project in accordance with the Plans and Specifications, the GMP Contract, the Approved Budget and the construction schedule, on or before the Outside Completion Date; (b) the funding of all costs of such completion in excess of the Loan proceeds, Retainage, contingency and Equity Contributions, without regard to any cost overrun, change order, casualty, Defect, contractor default, Insolvency Event affecting the Contractor or the Architect, or any other circumstance; and (c) payment of all amounts necessary to obtain the final, unconditional certificate of occupancy and to discharge all Liens (other than Permitted Exceptions). The Completion Guaranty shall remain in full force and effect until Lender has received evidence satisfactory to it that Final Completion has occurred. The Completion Guaranty is not limited in amount.

## Section 13.2 Carry Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several carry guaranty (the "**Carry Guaranty**") pursuant to which the Guarantors shall guarantee the payment of interest and all other carrying costs on the Loan during the term of the Loan, including (a) monthly interest, (b) real estate taxes and assessments, (c) insurance premiums, (d) the costs of completing the Project, (e) the reasonable costs of maintaining and operating the Property during any period of suspension or after an Event of Default, and (f) all Interest Reserve Shortfalls funded by Lender. The Carry Guaranty is in addition to, and not in lieu of, the Interest Reserve and shall apply to interest and carrying costs accruing after the Interest Reserve is exhausted or to the extent the Interest Reserve is insufficient.

## Section 13.3 Partial Repayment Guaranty

Each Guarantor shall execute and deliver to Lender, at Closing, a joint and several partial repayment guaranty (the "**Partial Repayment Guaranty**") in the maximum aggregate amount of $11,875,000, being twenty-five percent (25%) of the original principal amount of the Loan (the "**Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount**"). The Partial Repayment Guaranty is a guarantee of payment and not of collection. The Guarantors shall be jointly and severally liable for the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount, meaning that each Guarantor is individually liable for the full Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount (and not merely for a pro rata share), **provided** that Lender shall not be entitled to recover more than the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount in the aggregate from all Guarantors under the Partial Repayment Guaranty. The Partial Repayment Guaranty shall become due and payable upon (a) the occurrence of an Event of Default and acceleration of the Loan, (b) the commencement of any foreclosure or other enforcement proceeding, or (c) the Maturity Date, whichever first occurs.

## Section 13.4 Recourse Triggers

Notwithstanding **Section 13.3**, the liability of the Guarantors under the Partial Repayment Guaranty shall become full recourse for the entire amount of the Obligations (and not merely the Partial Repayment Guaranty Amount), less any amounts recovered by Lender from the realization on the collateral, upon the occurrence of any of the following (each, a "**Recourse Trigger**"): (a) fraud, intentional misrepresentation or willful misconduct by Borrower, any Guarantor, any member of Borrower or any Affiliate of any of the foregoing in connection with the Loan or the Loan Documents; (b) the voluntary filing by Borrower of a petition under the Bankruptcy Code or any other insolvency proceeding, or the consent by Borrower to the appointment of a receiver, trustee or custodian, or the collusive or bad-faith failure by Borrower to contest an involuntary petition; (c) any prohibited transfer, encumbrance, pledge or hypothecation of the Property, any membership interest in Borrower or any other collateral in violation of this Agreement, or any transfer that results in a change of control of Borrower; (d) any breach of the SPE covenants in **Article 18** or of the covenant to maintain the Independent Manager; (e) any Environmental Violation, any release of Hazardous Materials caused or permitted by Borrower, its agents or contractors, or any failure to comply with the NFA Letter, the Soil Management Plan or the Environmental Laws; (f) waste, arson, intentional destruction of the Property, or misapplication of insurance proceeds, condemnation awards, rents or security deposits; (g) the failure to complete the Project or the abandonment of the Project; (h) the misapplication or diversion of Loan proceeds, including any use of proceeds in violation of **Section 2.2**; (i) any amendment, modification or refinancing of the Mezzanine Loan in violation of **Section 25.6** or the Intercreditor Agreement; and (j) Borrower's assertion in any proceeding that any Loan Document is unenforceable or that the Loan is nonrecourse. Lender may pursue the Guarantors for the full amount of the Obligations upon the occurrence of a Recourse Trigger, and the Guarantors shall not be entitled to any reduction for the value of the collateral or for any nonrecourse limitation contained in any Loan Document.
